panels.title: Headline — is the resolver healthy and fast?
Request rate
panels.description: Total resolver requests per second across all routes.

panels.title: Error rate (5xx)
panels.description: 5xx as a fraction of all requests. 4xx is EXCLUDED on purpose: a caller sending bad input is not the resolver failing.

panels.title: p99 latency (all routes)
panels.description: 99th percentile across every route.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: hit / (hit + miss). 'bypass' is excluded — that means caching is switched OFF by config, which is a different state from a cache that never hits.

panels.title: Resolver pods up
panels.description: Scrape targets responding. Zero here means the resolver is gone — its own error rate would read as zero, not as broken.

panels.title: Caching enabled?
panels.description: Non-zero means CACHE_ENABLED is false. Without this panel a disabled cache is indistinguishable from one that never hits.

panels.title: CPU: usage vs limit
panels.description: Chart default limit is 250m. If usage pins to the limit under load, the capacity number measures the CONTAINER, not the software — resize and re-measure before quoting a ceiling.

panels.title: CPU throttling
panels.description: Seconds of throttling per second. Sustained non-zero means the CPU limit is the bottleneck, not the code.

panels.title: Memory: working set vs limit
panels.description: Working set is what the OOM killer reads. Default limit is 256Mi.

panels.title: Node heap: used vs total
panels.description: V8's own view, which the container metric cannot give. Heap climbing while RSS stays flat is normal; both climbing without falling after GC is a leak.

panels.title: GC pause time
panels.description: Seconds spent in GC per second — the fraction of wall clock lost to collection. Split by kind: a rising `major` share is the one that hurts latency.

panels.title: GC rate by kind
panels.description: Collections per second. Minor GC rising with load is expected; major GC rising is memory pressure.

panels.title: Event loop lag (p99)
panels.description: How long a callback waits to run. This is where CPU starvation and long GC pauses show up as request latency, and it moves BEFORE the route histograms do.

panels.title: GC pause p99
panels.description: Worst-case single pause. A long major-GC pause stalls every in-flight request at once.

panels.title: Handles and file descriptors
panels.description: Handles that only ever climb are a leak — sockets or timers never released. fds against max catches exhaustion under concurrency.

panels.title: p50 by route
panels.description: Median per route. 'route' is the controller method name, so it matches the request log line.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, route) (rate(vg_resource_resolver_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(vg_resource_resolver_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p99 by route
panels.description: The tail. A brown-out shows here before it becomes a timeout at the caller.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, route) (rate(vg_resource_resolver_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Rate by status class
panels.description: 2xx / 4xx / 5xx. Bucketed rather than raw codes: alerting needs 'is the resolver failing' separated from 'is a caller sending bad input'.

panels.title: Hit ratio by cached function
panels.description: Per-method, because the cache policy is per-method. A degraded ratio inflates MySQL load without failing a single call — the failure mode call-level success masks.

targets.expr: sum by (fn) (rate(vg_resource_resolver_cache_operations_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", result="hit"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (fn) (rate(vg_resource_resolver_cache_operations_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", result=~"hit|miss"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.001)

panels.title: Passthrough wired?
panels.description: 1 when at least one linked AI cluster is configured. A steady 0 on a cluster that is meant to be linked means every runtime-tenancy call is failing closed with a 502 — see the unconfigured-rejection panel below.

panels.title: Double-claims (1h)
panels.description: CRITICAL whenever non-zero. Two linked AI clusters both claimed the same call, so the answer was decided by a race — the same request can resolve to a different tenant's configuration run to run. Should be zero forever.

panels.title: Allowlisted but unclaimed (1h)
panels.description: An account in RUNTIME_TENANT_ACCOUNTS that every linked AI cluster disclaimed. The runtime arm does not fall back, so each one is a rejected call and a steady rate is a total outage for that tenant.

panels.title: Unconfigured rejections (1h)
panels.description: Requests the tenancy flag routed to the runtime path while no passthrough is wired. Each is a 502, and they are thrown before the timing wrapper runs — so requests_total never sees them.

panels.title: AI upstream error rate
panels.description: Share of resolveRuntimeResources calls to vg-runtime-api that failed. Includes fail-closed 502s.

panels.title: AI upstream p99
panels.description: Latency of the call into the AI cluster. This sits on the call-admission path, so it is added to every resolve that reaches the runtime arm.

panels.title: Upstream calls by outcome
panels.description: resolveRuntimeResources calls into vg-runtime-api. `error` covers every RuntimeApiError, including the fail-closed 502s.

panels.title: Upstream latency percentiles
panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of the cross-cluster call. 017 objected to per-call fan-out on latency grounds; this is the number that settles it.

panels.title: Per-target attempts by outcome
panels.description: Each linked AI cluster, split by what it answered. `unauthorized` on one target and not others is a trust-list problem on that cluster; `unavailable` is a transport fault. `miss` is the normal not-my-account answer.

panels.title: AI clusters queried per resolve
panels.description: Since the fan-out went concurrent this is the configured width rather than a count of sequential attempts, so it is near-constant per deployment. Kept because the width IS the AI-side load multiplier, and it moving is worth seeing.

panels.title: Admission decisions by outcome
panels.description: resolveCallAdmission results. `admitted` is the happy path; everything else is the rejection reason, or `error`.

panels.title: Admission decisions by originator
panels.description: Which caller the decision was for — trunk, client, and so on. A rejection spike confined to one originator is a different problem from one across all of them.

panels.title: Comparisons, and how many diverged
panels.description: The shadow path runs detached and never affects the answer. `discrepant=true` means the two paths disagreed on at least one contract field.

panels.title: Shadow errors by originator
panels.description: The shadow path threw instead of returning a result. Harmless to the call — it is fire-and-forget — but it means the comparison is blind, so divergence below is under-reported.

panels.title: Divergent fields
panels.description: Which contract field actually differed. This is the panel that says WHAT to fix before a cutover — a single field dominating is usually one mapping, not a broken path.
